events.title: Granada Surrenders, Ending Moorish Rule in Spain
events.description: Granada, the last Muslim-ruled kingdom on the Iberian Peninsula, fell to the forces of King Ferdinand and Queen Isabella. The surrender ended roughly eight centuries of Moorish presence in Spain.
events.significance: The fall of Granada completed the Spanish Reconquista and unified Spain under Catholic monarchs. The same monarchs sponsored Columbus's voyage later that year.

events.title: Union Victory at the Battle of Stones River
events.description: The three-day Battle of Stones River in Tennessee ended when Confederate forces under General Braxton Bragg were repulsed for the last time by Union troops under General William Rosecrans.
events.significance: It was one of the bloodiest battles of the Civil War relative to the number of troops engaged. The Union victory gave Northern morale a lift and secured central Tennessee.

events.title: Birth of Isaac Asimov
events.description: Isaac Asimov was born in Petrovichi, in Soviet Russia, and came to the United States with his family as a small child. He became one of the most prolific and influential writers of the 20th century.
events.significance: Asimov's science fiction, including the Foundation and Robot stories, shaped how generations imagined the future. His popular science writing also made complex ideas accessible to ordinary readers.

events.title: Luna 1 Launched Toward the Moon
events.description: The Soviet Union launched Luna 1 from the Baikonur Cosmodrome. It became the first spacecraft to escape Earth's gravity and pass by the Moon, then entered orbit around the Sun.
events.significance: Luna 1 was a milestone of the early Space Race. It showed that deep-space travel was possible and paved the way for later lunar missions.

events.title: Nixon Signs the National Speed Limit into Law
events.description: President Richard Nixon signed the Emergency Highway Energy Conservation Act, which set a national maximum speed limit across the United States during the energy crisis.
events.significance: The law, which became known as the 55 mph limit, was a response to oil shortages. It affected American driving for more than two decades and sparked lasting debate about road safety and fuel conservation.
